claim: GitHub Actions supports cron-scheduled workflows, and this repo runs its blog on exactly that — free, with no server.
detail: A YAML file with a cron expression is a scheduler: the engine wakes up, researches, writes, publishes, and commits the result. Public repos get unlimited minutes, and the same workflow file gives the owner a one-click 'run now' button in the Actions tab.
steps: Add on: schedule: - cron: '17 6 * * *' to a workflow
Checkout the repo and run the engine in the job
Commit generated content so the static host deploys it

claim: Google Search Console is free and it is the single most valuable SEO tool there is.
detail: Verify the site (a file or DNS record — both free), submit the sitemap, and you get the queries that actually bring people, the pages that rank, and indexing problems caught early. Nothing on a paid SEO stack replaces this data, and it costs nothing.
steps: Add the site property and verify with a DNS TXT record or verification file
Check Performance weekly — note the queries worth writing more about

claim: Bing Webmaster Tools is the free, often-overlooked sibling of Search Console — and Bing's index is also used by Copilot.
detail: Verification is one DNS record, sitemap submission is one click, and you get indexing status plus traffic data for the second-largest engine. Fifteen minutes of setup, zero dollars, meaningful extra reach.

claim: JSON-LD structured data (Schema.org) is a free standard that tells search engines exactly what your page is.
detail: Marking a post as an Article with author and dates, and marking its FAQ block as a FAQPage, is what powers rich results. It is a machine-readable summary the page already contains — no service, no cost, and this engine generates it for every post it writes.

claim: A sitemap.xml is a free, standard index of your pages that crawlers use to find everything you publish.
detail: Each entry is a URL plus last-modified date; search consoles ingest it in seconds. For an autonomous blog it is mandatory plumbing — every new post must appear in it, and the engine rebuilds it on every publish so it never goes stale.

claim: You can do real keyword research with free, keyless endpoints — this blog's own research runs on them.
detail: Autocomplete suggestions reveal what people actually type; question-mark queries reveal intent; and cross-source agreement (the same phrase suggested by two of three search engines) is a cheap signal of demand. Pair that with Search Console data once live and you have a keyword pipeline with a zero-dollar budget.

claim: pytrends is an open-source Python client for Google Trends — free programmatic access to interest-over-time data.
detail: It wraps the unofficial Trends API, so it can break when Google changes things, but it is the standard way to check whether a topic's interest is rising before you commit the blog to a topic family. Use it as a trend check, not a firehose.

claim: APScheduler is the open-source Python library for scheduling jobs in-process — cron triggers, intervals, one-liners.
detail: If the engine runs on a long-lived box instead of GitHub Actions, APScheduler is the free cron replacement: add a trigger, register a job, run the loop. It is what makes 'the blog wakes up on its own' a single dependency-free file.

claim: SQLite is the most deployed database in the world — free, public domain, and a single file.
detail: For a self-hosted stack it removes an entire class of infrastructure: no server process, no connection pool, no backup job (copy the file). Full-text search is built in, which is plenty for a personal content database.

claim: The difference between 'scraping' and 'being blocked' is politeness: identify yourself, rate-limit, and cache.
detail: A descriptive User-Agent, a few seconds between requests, honoring robots.txt, and caching responses are the whole etiquette. Most sites allow reasonable personal-use access; the keyless endpoints this engine uses are the same ones the search boxes use, and they reward clients who behave.
steps: Set a descriptive User-Agent with contact info
Space requests (this engine sleeps between outbound calls)
Cache results per query — never re-fetch what you already have
